correctness.rationale: For H=d(zI-P), the final Chebyshev inverse polynomial equals [T_m(z)-T_m(P)]/[d T_m(z)(zI-P)]. Exact divided differences have nonnegative coefficients for degrees 1..4 and for degree 5 if z>=sqrt(5)/2, i.e. kappa<=9+4sqrt(5). For any z in (1,sqrt(5)/2), the Q_d neighboring entry equals 16z/[d^2 T_5(z)](z^2-5/4+(3d-2)/d^2), and is negative for a finite sufficiently large d. Adding a small positive constant vector makes the right-hand side strictly positive while keeping that entry negative. A separate exact-rational program replayed 572 finite checks; the all-d proof is algebraic, not experimental.

value.rationale: The first failing iteration degree and the sharp condition-number barrier are natural exact invariants of preserving a physical nonnegative solution cone under widely used Chebyshev inverse polynomial iteration. The result applies to an infinite graph family, gives a sufficient and necessary graph-uniform design condition, and constructs positive-data failures despite a positive exact solution. It is not a mere consequence of finite numerical tests or cosmetic renaming; its limitation to m<=5 is explicit.
